images.title: Permissioned vs permissionless leverage
images.alt: Comparison of Naval Ravikant's permissioned leverage, capital and labor, with permissionless leverage, code and media you can make without asking.
images.caption: Only the making is permissionless. Getting found still runs through platforms.

columns.label: Permissioned
points: Someone has to hand you the money
Or agree to work for you

columns.label: Permissionless
points: You can make it without asking anyone

images.title: What leverage costs
images.alt: Four cards on the costs of leveraged assets: you pay before you know, content decays, code decays, and every asset needs a review date.
images.caption: Upkeep is still far less work than serving every reader or user by hand.

items.title: You pay first
items.text: An article can take months to rank, if at all; a tool can launch to nobody

items.title: Content decays
items.text: Prices and details go stale, competitors publish better, results shift

items.title: Code decays
items.text: Libraries update, security holes appear, platforms and APIs change rules

items.title: Budget for upkeep
items.text: Put a review date on every asset the day you publish it

images.after: How to decide what to build first
images.title: Choosing your first asset
images.alt: Five steps to pick a first leveraged asset: list repeated questions, check demand, build the smallest version, give it a window, then review the numbers.
images.caption: Most first assets won't earn much. The first one teaches you how long things take.

items.title: List repeated questions
items.text: Ones you've answered more than twice, for clients, in forums or for yourself

items.title: Check others ask too
items.text: Keyword research for content; test the idea before building a tool

items.title: Build the smallest version
items.text: One article before an ebook. A spreadsheet before an app

items.title: Give it a fixed window
items.text: Put it where people already look and wait, say three months

items.title: Review the numbers
items.text: Improve it, leave it or drop it, then set the next review date
